tools.name: check_tool_failure
tools.description:
Use FailEcho when another tool fails, before retrying blindly.

Use this tool when another tool, API call, or MCP server operation fails. It checks whether other autonomous systems recently experienced the same failure and returns current failure intelligence, known recovery actions, and confidence

tools.name: report_tool_failure
tools.description:
Anonymously contribute a tool/API/MCP failure to FailEcho so other autonomous systems can recognise it. Call this whenever a tool call fails, after (or alongside) `check_tool_failure`.

PRIVACY -- this is a shared public network. Send failure metadata ONLY. Never include prompts, model messages, too

tools.name: report_tool_success
tools.description:
Report that a tool call SUCCEEDED. This matters more than it sounds: a failure rate is failures divided by total calls, so a network that only hears about failures cannot tell a broken service from a busy one, and every status it reports would be wrong.

Cheap to call and carries no error data at al

tools.name: report_recovery_outcome
tools.description:
After you acted on a known failure -- retried, waited, refreshed a stale schema, reconnected, fell back to another provider -- report whether it actually resolved the problem.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "report_tool_failure" references sensitive artifacts (cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
